title: Vikings owner says 'patience isn't infinite' as he discusses team's lack of postseason success
text:
Vikings owner says 'patience isn't infinite' as he discusses team's lack of postseason success
The Vikings have been competitive since the Wilfs bought the franchise in 2005, but they have won only three playoff games in that time.
(Vikings owner Mark Wilf addresses the media on Wednesday at TCO Performance Center.)
Kevin O’Connell enters his fifth season as Vikings coach with a 43-25 regular-season record, giving him the highest-winning percentage (.632) of any coach in franchise history. His resume includes two seasons in which the Vikings reached double-digit victories and made the postseason.
But that regular-season success has not carried over into the playoffs. The Vikings have yet to win a postseason game under O’Connell — they lost to the Giants and Rams in the first round in 2022 and 2024, respectively — and the team has not made back-to-back playoff appearances since 2008 and 2009.
While O’Connell is the face of the Vikings’ recent woes, the role of ownership can’t be ignored. The Vikings have made eight trips to the playoffs since Mark and Zygi Wilf bought the franchise in 2005, and Minnesota has won three playoff games in that time.
There were NFC Divisional wins in 2009 and 2017 — those seasons ended in losses in the conference title game — and a first-round win over New Orleans in 2019. That is the Vikings’ last playoff victory, and it came under Mike Zimmer.
“Ultimately, it's about not just playoff wins, but championships, and that is the ultimate measure,” Mark Wilf said Wednesday when asked about the lack of postseason success. “We know that. We try to be patient as an ownership (group), and that, we know, is the ultimate success; but, of course, patience isn't infinite. We understand that, but I feel really good about the direction of this football club, and we're going to get those benchmarks checked off here.”
The question many Viking fans have for the Wilf: When is that going to happen?
On Jan. 9, 2027, the Vikings will reach 50 years without having reached the Super Bowl. On that date in 1977, the Vikings lost to the Oakland Raiders, 32-14, leaving them without a Super Bowl victory in four trips (1970, 1974, 1975). The Vikings have been to the NFC title game six times since and suffered defeats in a variety of agonizing ways. The Wilfs were owners for two of them.
The Wilfs have never steered clear of discussing their desire to hoist the Lombardi Trophy, and they have consistently invested in the product in order to achieve that goal. But it has yet to happen, and any Vikings fan under the age of 54 or 55 probably has no memory of that last trip to the Super Bowl.
Vikings ownership has put its faith in O’Connell to get the team back to the Super Bowl, but first he’s going to have to prove he can win a playoff game. The decision to hire general manager Nolan Teasley away from the Seattle Seahawks in June is considered a positive step by Mark Wilf. Of course, feeling that Kwesi Adofo-Mensah had to be fired as GM in January after only four seasons on the job wasn’t part of the plan.
